clue.text: Definitely not smart to cross river in wood

indicators.note: to cross something here is to lie across it, so one piece sits inside the phrase it spans

blocks.note: no way is an emphatic refusal
R is the standard abbreviation for river
spruce means neat and smart in appearance

explanation.surface: Someone scruffy wading across a river through a forest is hardly well turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' looks like the forest of the surface, but it means timber; the answer is a tree species prized for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway spruce is a common conifer whose timber is widely used, so it is an example of a wood.

clue.text: Squeezed between poles, shaft becomes smaller

indicators.note: something squeezed between two things is held inside them

blocks.note: the north and south poles, N and S
an arrow is a shaft shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A mine shaft squeezed between supports gets tighter.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrow is to grow less wide, so narrows means becomes smaller in breadth.

clue.text: Reply on legislative document

blocks.note: re means on or concerning, as in letter headings
an Act is a law passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: A formal response is given to a piece of legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something, so it works as the verb reply.

clue.text: Showing up late in the evening perhaps, lot of noise generated at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: at ten o'clock is one late evening time, hence the 'perhaps'
a din is a great deal of loud noise
first letter of generated

explanation.surface: A guest arrives late in the evening and makes a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late in the evening' is only one example time, which the 'perhaps' admits; ten o'clock is the setter's pick.
explanation.definitionFit: Attending an event means being present at it, which is the same as showing up there.

clue.text: Basic construction dropped

blocks.note: first meaning: a simple hut or outbuilding
second meaning: cast off, as a snake loses its skin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a simple building being abandoned; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a plain wooden outbuilding, and shed is also the past tense of a verb meaning to let fall.

clue.text: Rocky mineral broken by fine soldier

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaky, so the letters of the word next to it get jumbled
a word broken by another has that other piece forced into its middle

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A soldier smashes some rock-bound mineral ore.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifleman is an infantry soldier armed with a rifle, so he is a type of soldier.

clue.text: What motorist after breakdown might be heard shouting a load?

blocks.clueFragment: What motorist after breakdown might be heard shouting
blocks.note: surface reading: a stranded driver yelling at a dead engine
setter's reading: the driver's two-word plea to the vehicle to move runs together into a word for goods carried

explanation.surface: A frustrated driver whose car has broken down yells at it to move.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it is exactly what the driver would bellow at the stalled vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is goods carried by a ship, plane or lorry, so it is a load being transported.

clue.text: Impressive punching

blocks.note: first meaning: eye-catching, remarkable
second meaning: hitting with a blow

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise for a boxer's punches; the two words are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking describes something that makes a strong impression, and is also the present participle of strike, to hit.

clue.text: Food centre stretched to provide tea

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, with the outer ones stripped away

blocks.note: the two middle letters of food
something stretched is made long

explanation.surface: Pulling out the middle of a meal to make a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Oolong is a partly fermented Chinese tea, so it is a variety of tea.

clue.text: Criticise grouse meat

blocks.note: to roast someone is to criticise them harshly
a beef is a complaint or grouse

explanation.surface: Someone complains about game birds served as a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like the game bird on the plate; it is the complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is a classic cooked joint, so it is a kind of meat dish.

clue.text: Reminiscent of the past, inferior terraced houses, west-facing

indicators.note: a phrase that houses something contains it within its run of letters
in an across clue, facing west means reading right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned, run-down terraced homes facing west.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro styles deliberately imitate fashions from earlier decades, so they recall the past.

clue.text: Don't start selling excursion

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter of the next word is removed

blocks.note: touting is selling, especially pushily or on the black market

explanation.surface: An instruction to a trader to hold off selling tours.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short trip for pleasure, a synonym for an excursion.

clue.text: Cheese poor, nice crackers

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheese board judged: the cheese is poor, but the biscuits are nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like the biscuits served with cheese; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecorino is a hard Italian cheese made from sheep's milk.

clue.text: Turn right entering country

indicators.note: a piece entering a word goes inside it

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
a European country

explanation.surface: A driving direction: take a right turn into a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reads as a driving direction; it is the definition, a twist of a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprain an ankle is to twist or wrench it, which is what turning it awkwardly means.

clue.text: Sergeant doctored substances found in laboratory

indicators.note: doctored means tampered with, so the letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An army sergeant tampers with chemicals in a lab.
explanation.definitionFit: Reagents are chemicals used to cause or detect reactions, the stock of any laboratory.

clue.text: Making tuneful sound, flashy armour?

blocks.note: first meaning: singing with trills, like a bird
whimsical second reading: showy jewellery, or bling, worn for battle

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as WAR BLING: bling is slang for showy jewellery, so battle bling is flashy armour. The question mark flags the invented phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Warbling is singing with trills and quavers, as songbirds do, so it is producing a melodious sound.

clue.text: Seers bald, surprisingly clean-shaven

indicators.note: surprisingly signals an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Prophets are bald and, unexpectedly, have no beards either.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clean-shaven has no facial hair, so they are without a beard.

clue.text: Flower border: tedious stuff written about that

indicators.note: one piece goes about, or around, the thing just named

blocks.note: prose is ordinary written text, and prosy means dull
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A dull essay about a garden border of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' refers back to the border, which sits inside the dull writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring flower of woods and hedgerows.

clue.text: Veterans maintaining good condition in horses

indicators.note: something maintaining another piece holds it, keeping it inside

blocks.note: old stagers are experienced veterans
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Old hands keep horses in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good condition' looks like one phrase; good is the G and condition belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The staggers is a disease of horses and livestock that causes a reeling gait.

clue.text: Perfect prize scooped by boy

indicators.note: something scooped by another is held up inside it

blocks.note: a son is a boy
a pot is a prize or trophy cup

explanation.surface: A boy wins the perfect prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is an informal phrase for exactly right, the same as perfect.

clue.text: Engineer beginning on wrong corner

indicators.note: the beginning on a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of wrong
an angle is a corner

explanation.surface: An engineer starts building on the wrong corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a noun; it is the verb, to contrive something.
explanation.definitionFit: To wangle something is to obtain it by cunning, just as to engineer it is to arrange it craftily.

clue.text: Level he once managed, to inspire learner

indicators.note: something managed is handled and arranged, so the letters are put in a new order
to inspire is literally to breathe in, so a piece is drawn inside

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A former manager once reached a level that inspired a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a rank or tier in an organisation, so it means a level.

clue.text: Best series of deliveries arrive

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: The best set of deliveries turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' reads as an adjective; it is the verb meaning to defeat. An over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat them, which is what overcome means.

clue.text: What's carried by responsible type on principle

blocks.note: whoever carries the can takes the responsibility
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dutiful person carries out a task on principle.
explanation.walkthrough: To carry the can is a British idiom for taking the blame or responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a general rule or standard by which things are judged, so it means a principle.

clue.text: Quite strange sending back party food

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, read backwards

blocks.note: a do is a party
a dish is a prepared item of food

explanation.surface: It is rather odd to send the party food back.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means somewhat, so oddish means somewhat odd or strange.

clue.text: I complain endlessly about queen from Basra, say?

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off
about means going around, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: taken as written
to rail is to complain bitterly
Q is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a queen who comes from Basra.
explanation.walkthrough: Rail loses its end to leave RAI, which wraps around Q.
explanation.definitionFit: Basra is a city in Iraq, so a person or thing from there is an example of Iraqi.

clue.text: Stop NY baseball team going up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the New York Mets are a baseball team

explanation.surface: Stopping a New York baseball team on the rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to check or halt it, a synonym for stop.

clue.text: Cushion trimmed at the front in many cases

indicators.note: trimming at the front cuts away the opening letter

blocks.note: to cushion a blow is to soften it

explanation.surface: A cushion that has been trimmed at its front edge, as happens a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cushion' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to soften.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done often happens frequently, so it happens in many cases.

clue.text: Alert, looking to pass or shoot?

blocks.note: first meaning: quick-witted and well informed
second meaning, literal: a footballer in possession, ready to pass or shoot

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the literal reading of an idiom: a player with the ball at their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: On the ball is an idiom for alert and quick to react, and literally describes a player in possession.

clue.text: Italian team calling for half-time?

blocks.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club
a mission is a vocation or calling

explanation.surface: An Italian football team's manager speaking at half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' looks like shouting; it is a vocation. The question mark marks half-time as one example of a break.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermission is a break between parts of a performance or match, and half-time is one such break.
